name: Wealthsimple
desc: Canadian online investment platform offering self-directed trading, managed portfolios, crypto, savings and tax filing to retail clients.

name: Cohesity
desc: Venture-backed data protection and security software company that acquired Veritas Technologies in December 2024; about 6,000 employees.

name: Dun & Bradstreet
desc: Business data and analytics company supplying commercial credit, risk and sales data on companies worldwide, taken private by Clearlake in 2025.

name: Bullhorn
desc: Cloud software provider for staffing and recruiting firms offering CRM, applicant tracking and operations management, with offices in North America, Europe and Australia.

name: Audio-Technica
desc: Privately held Japanese maker of headphones, microphones, wireless audio systems, turntables and phono cartridges, and an Olympic audio supplier.

name: General Atlantic
desc: New York growth equity investor with about USD 125 billion under management, over 900 staff and a presence in 20 countries.

name: Trilux
desc: Family-controlled German maker of technical luminaires, outdoor and street lighting and lighting electronics, German market leader for technical lights.

name: Normal
desc: Danish discount chain founded in 2013 selling branded beauty, personal-care and household goods in more than 1,000 stores across 14 European countries.

name: Hutchinson
desc: French maker of sealing, fluid-management, vibration-control and materials systems, a TotalEnergies subsidiary since 1970 with 40,000 staff in 26 countries.

name: Crown Equipment Corporation
desc: Privately held maker of electric forklift trucks and warehouse material-handling equipment, with plants in the US, Germany, Mexico, China and Australia.

name: Avanade
desc: Seattle-based Microsoft technology consultancy formed by Accenture and Microsoft in 2000, operating in 26 countries with about USD 4bn revenue.

name: Blum Group
desc: Austrian family-owned maker of furniture fittings such as hinges, lift systems and drawer runners, exporting about 97% of output.

name: Rosenberger
desc: Family-owned German supplier of high-frequency, fibre-optic and high-voltage connectivity for automotive, telecom, medical and aerospace.

name: Cloud Imperium Games
desc: Developer of the crowdfunded space simulation Star Citizen and Squadron 42, with studios in the UK, US, Germany and Canada.

name: FEV Group
desc: Family-run Aachen engineering-services group developing powertrain, e-drive, battery, fuel-cell and vehicle technology for the world's largest carmakers and other mobility sectors.

name: Avia Solutions Group
desc: Founder-controlled aviation services group providing ACMI wet leasing, charter, MRO, training and cargo brokerage with over 200 aircraft.

name: Action
desc: European non-food discount retailer with over 3,400 stores in 15 countries, majority-owned by 3i Group, planning US entry.

name: Clayton, Dubilier & Rice
desc: New York private equity firm pairing operating executives with investors to buy and improve large industrial, services, healthcare and consumer businesses.

name: Hg
desc: London investor specialising in software and business-services buyouts across Europe and North America, ranked sixth in the PEI 300.

name: HongShan
desc: Venture, growth and buyout investor formerly Sequoia Capital China, backing consumer, technology and healthcare companies with about USD 61 billion.

name: Despegar
desc: Latin America's leading online travel agency selling flights, hotels and packages in about 20 countries, owned by Prosus since May 2025.

name: Nordic Capital
desc: Private equity firm with about USD 50 billion, whose recent deals include selling Clario to Thermo Fisher and taking Hargreaves Lansdown private.

name: Software AG
desc: German enterprise software company, now Software GmbH under Silver Lake, owning ARIS process mining and Adabas & Natural mainframe database businesses.

name: Farallon Capital Management
desc: San Francisco investment firm founded in 1986, managing about USD 42 billion, with offices in Sao Paulo, Tokyo, Singapore and London.

name: Canyon Bicycles
desc: German direct-to-consumer maker of road, gravel, mountain and e-bikes, supplying several UCI WorldTour teams.

name: Zott
desc: Independent Bavarian family dairy producing Zottarella, Monte and Jogobella, with plants in Germany and Poland and sales units in Central Europe and Vietnam.

name: EF Education First
desc: Family-owned international education company offering language training, study abroad, educational travel and academic programmes in over 100 countries.

name: Schmitz Cargobull
desc: Family-owned German maker of semi-trailers, trailers and truck bodies with leasing, parts, telematics and used-vehicle services.

name: Heitman
desc: Chicago real estate investment manager ranked among the world's twenty largest, with about USD 47 billion of real estate assets.

name: Ivanhoe Cambridge
desc: Montreal real estate investment company ranked among the world's twenty largest real estate managers, with about USD 56 billion (2023).

name: LaSalle Investment Management
desc: Chicago real estate investment manager ranked eleventh worldwide by real estate assets, with about USD 87 billion at end-2025.

name: TA Associates
desc: Boston private equity firm with about USD 55 billion under management and offices in Menlo Park, Austin, London, Mumbai and Hong Kong.

name: Diriyah Company
desc: PIF-owned developer of the USD 50bn Diriyah giga-project, a heritage, hospitality, retail and residential destination on Riyadh's edge.

name: Riyadh Air
desc: PIF-owned Saudi flag carrier that began commercial flights in October 2025 and has ordered over 150 Airbus and Boeing aircraft.

name: TAP Air Portugal
desc: Portuguese state-owned flag carrier linking Lisbon with Europe, Brazil, Africa and North America, now being partly sold to Lufthansa.

name: SUSE
desc: Enterprise open-source software company providing SUSE Linux Enterprise, container and edge platforms, owned by EQT after its 2023 Frankfurt delisting.

name: Hillhouse Investment
desc: Singapore-headquartered investment firm founded by Lei Zhang in 2005, managing about USD 100 billion across Asia, the US, UK and Abu Dhabi.

name: Haldiram's
desc: Family-owned Indian maker of namkeen snacks, sweets and ready meals that also runs restaurants; Temasek invested in 2025.

name: Syntegon
desc: German processing and packaging machinery group for pharma and food, the former Bosch packaging division owned by CVC since 2019.

name: Keywords Studios
desc: Global provider of art, engineering, testing, localisation, audio and player-support services to video game publishers, taken private by EQT in 2024.
